news.titulo: We built a mobile platformer where you can't control the jump
news.resumen: We’re continuing to take our game experiment into new environments. After moving the discussion into developer communities, we’ve now also brought Crom’s Escape onto TapTap — a platform directly focused on mobile gamers. Same idea, different audience.

news.titulo: [GAME][DEV] I built a platformer where jumping is automatic – curious how it plays
news.resumen: We’re continuing to take our game experiment into real communities. After sharing our approach here and gathering initial feedback, we’ve now also started engaging on XDA Developers — one of the largest Android and developer-driven platforms. Instead of focusing on promotion, we deliberately put the core idea up for discussion: a mobile platformer where you can’t control the jump.

news.titulo: Another German PR platform where “Crom’s Escape” is now featured.
news.resumen: After publishing and approval of our article on Online-Pressemitteilung.de, we received the following message: “The entry was successful. […] If you have your own homepage, please consider linking back to our portal […] This will help increase visibility and ensure your article is noticed more frequently.” We would like to take this opportunity to respond — and to sincerely thank the platform operators for including our content.

news.titulo: Crom’s Escape: Android-Platformer mit automatischer Sprungmechanik erschienen
news.resumen: Crom’s Escape is slowly starting to appear across different platforms and contexts. A short piece about the game is now also featured on another German press portal, called “Firmenpresse”, focusing on its core idea and gameplay approach. It’s interesting to see how the same concept is presented depending on the context — from dev discussions to more general publications.

news.titulo: Designing a platformer where you don’t control jumping
news.resumen: Jumping is usually the core mechanic of a platformer. It defines how the player interacts with the world. It’s reactive, immediate, and deeply ingrained in how these games are typically played. So we started with a simple question: What happens if you remove that control completely?

news.titulo: Designing a platformer where you don’t control jumping
news.resumen: We recently released a 2D precision platformer on Android, built around a simple question: What happens if the player doesn't control jumping? In most platformers, jumping is the core mechanic. It’s reactive and immediate. You press a button, and you jump.

news.titulo: Crom's Escape: Hard 2D Precision Platformer with Auto-Jump Mechanic Released on Android
news.resumen: Crom’s Escape has just appeared on another public stage where indie games can be discovered. 🚀 Our press release is now live on openPR, giving the project another public touchpoint beyond our own channels. For us, every new appearance helps strengthen context, credibility, and discoverability around the game.

news.titulo: Has anyone spotted our Crom’s Escape listing on IndieDB yet?
news.resumen: It probably hasn’t been live for very long, so we’re curious whether anyone has already come across it.

When we decide to showcase a project on a platform, it’s less about exposure and more about context. Game Jolt is a space where games are discovered through intent rather than algorithms. It’s where developers, players, and creators look at projects with curiosity for how they are built — not just how they are marketed.

news.titulo: Crom’s Escape was never designed to be a casual game
news.resumen: Instead of comfort or accessibility, we focused on precision, timing, and patience. In Crom’s Escape, jumping is automatic. Players control only movement, timing, and positioning. One mistake is often enough to fail. There is no difficulty slider. The challenge is not adjustable — it is intrinsic to the design.

news.titulo: Crom’s Escape Gets a Fresh Update on Google Play
news.resumen: Amphoteric Studio’s mobile platformer receives gameplay improvements, UI updates, and a new resurrection system in its latest patch.On May 6th, Crom’s Escape, the mobile platformer developed by Amphoteric Game Studio, received a new update on Google Play focused on improving gameplay flow, controls, and the overall user experience.

We’re pleased to share that Crom’s Escape has been featured on QUDO as part of its latest Indie Game Drop. For Amphoteric, it’s a meaningful moment to see our debut title highlighted on a platform that celebrates independent games and creative studios.

news.titulo: Crom’s Escape Review: Amphoteric Studio’s Indie Game Debut
news.resumen: A few days ago, we downloaded and played Crom’s Escape, the debut release from Amphoteric Game Studio, and we also had the chance to speak with its creators. In this feature, we explore the inspiration behind the game along with the key challenges and opportunities facing indie game developers today.
